_purpose: STEP-CONTRACT-LAW (GAP-2026-11-04-STEP7-CONTRACT-RESTORE, owner decision D6, 2026-11-04). A step's USER CONTRACT — what the operator receives at the end, the states the step may end in, and the only actions it may ask of the operator — is DATA, machine-checked by mock_sync_audit MS-27 against the specs, DeliveryFooter, routes.json and both SKILL trigger lists. Release 2026.11.03 changed all three parts of Step 7's contract (a review packet instead of two files; an AWAITING_REVIEW end state; a new-chat review, a verdict file to carry back and a --resume to type) with no test and no explicit sign-off; every exam project on the estate inherited it on its next paper.
_change_rule: An entry here changes ONLY with an owner decision id cited in the same CHANGELOG.md entry (release checklist line: 'Does this release add a user action, a deliverable, or an end state to any step? If yes: owner decision id + updated STEP_CONTRACTS.json + a legacy-project end-to-end test'). A release that needs MS-27 relaxed to ship has changed a contract.

override_floor._note: Project-first spec resolution (spec_source.py) will NOT load a project Files copy of these specs whose version header is BELOW the floor: such a copy predates the Step 7 contract restore and would silently re-break it (a v5.90 Create ends at AWAITING_REVIEW; a v1.0.0 MockReview cannot read the internal packet). The verified repo copy is used and Step 0 prints [STALE — NOT LOADED]. Never a stop. Raise a floor only with an owner decision id (same rule as the contracts). Raised 2026-11-05 under owner decision D8 (GAP-2026-11-05-DIFFICULTY-FIDELITY): every spec that release edits gets a floor at its new version, so a project copy written before the difficulty fix is never loaded over it.
